Source assessment: the complete claim requires hierarchical prefix groups, reveal/hide of descendants, separate implementation/test subtree counts, and derivation from the displayed active anchors. In anchors.rs, names selects spec.anchors with exact-or-dot-boundary within matching; table derives and deduplicates each ancestor prefix and selects members from that same names vector. counts independently queries implementation and test status sets, preserving mixed statuses and counting each anchor once per applicable status. The ordinary association therefore supports hierarchy, membership and rendered counts. The complete associated integration test asserts meta/meta.foo groups, three active anchors, 1 Implemented/1 TODO/2 N/A, exact root and sibling memberships, and a rule that is also a namespace. Its explicit assertions would catch missing group markup, incorrect fixture totals or sibling leakage. Captured Fixture and chapters helpers construct a real temporary workspace, invoke the preprocessor, and recursively collect generated chapters. The other complete associated test and implementation entry, todo::anchor_index_prefix_groups, intentionally have no assertions and explicitly defer expand/collapse and exhaustive per-subtree count comparisons. This is a justified remaining gap, not passing behavioral evidence: completing it requires interactive DOM/browser tests over nested prefixes and comparisons of both count columns against actual descendants. Captured anchors.js supplies click wiring, strict-dot descendant hiding, disclosure state, and bulk toggles; this inspection does not discharge that explicit interactive TODO or establish browser execution. No N/A entry applies to this anchor.

Baseline verification: exact reconstructed-byte comparison confirms both historical spec_plan.rs snapshots match current source. anchors.rs changes are fragment-based test excerpts and review-output presentation; the grouping/counting functions are unchanged. book.rs changes adapt review setup and verify accepted/requested/unfinished displays, plus unrelated claim-fragment access; the grouping assertions remain unchanged. I independently reassessed the supplied historical rationale against these current inputs rather than treating it as current approval.

The coordinator-reported 321 passing tests and root build, and the historical focused test run, are separate execution evidence. All claim aspects are supported by inspected source/test assertions or the explicit retained TODO; no source edits requested.
